## Claims
- [source-backed] RWY Theorem 4.8 gives two integral generating families for \(J_v\): the right-adjoined and lower-adjoined families. [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 864-876]
- [source-backed] RWY Conjecture 4.10 asserts that both families are minimal. [doi:10.1090/s0002-9947-2010-05163-3, lines 938-946]
- [source-backed] St. Dizier–Yong Theorem 1.2, for \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), \(i=s-t+1\), \(j=r-t+1\), \(a=\min(n-r-i,r-j)\), \(b=\min(i,j)\), proves minimality only of \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}\) in \(H^*(\mathrm{Gr}_{r,n})\cong\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 213-235]
- [source-backed] The same paper’s Corollary 4.6 again formally concludes minimality only for the lower-adjoined family. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 819-831]
- [source-backed] Its Remark 4.7 identifies the right-adjoined family \(\{\bar s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}\) as conjugate to the proved family and says one “could straightforwardly” transpose the arguments; it does not state a transposed theorem or corollary. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 833-840]

## Strategy
Compared the original two-clause conjecture with the inspected 2024 full text. The requested target is established: the project’s proof of both clauses remains internal context, while the inspected 2024 literature formally proves only the lower-adjoined clause.

## Gaps
Bounded negative result only: among the inspected 2011 and 2024 full-text sources, no formal theorem for the right-adjoined clause was found. This is not a claim about uninspected literature.
